{{Quote|&hellip;I've moved to this sector to stay.''"<br />"''As if this place didn't stink enough without you.|Zodoh and a captive Jenn Devaad|<ref name="SWKE8">[[Knight Errant: Deluge 3|''Knight Errant: Deluge'' 3]]</ref>}}
'''Zodoh''' was a [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] during the later [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the [[New Sith Wars]], a conflict between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]], who profited by selling [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]] and munitions to the Sith based in [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]]. By [[1032 BBY/Legends|1032 BBY]], Zodoh had grown weary of the constant warfare between the Hutt [[Kajidic/Legends|clans]] and set out to expand his influence into the Sith-dominated [[Grumani sector/Legends|Grumani sector]]. The key to Zodoh's plans was his [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] of [[Stormdriver]]s, [[Starship/Legends|starships]] which were capable of harnessing [[Water/Legends|moisture]] from [[Planet/Legends|planetary]] [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmospheres]] and unleashing it as storms which could flood an entire world, wiping out all life. As a demonstration of his power to the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]] operating in the area, Zodoh [[Aquilaris campaign|tested]] his new weapon on the planet [[Aquilaris Minor]] in the [[Daimanate]], a region of [[Realspace/Legends|space]] controlled by the Sith [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Daiman]]. The Hutt was forced to abort the [[Great Aquilaris Deluge|operation]] early when [[Jenn Devaad]], a Republic [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] and former slave of Zodoh's, set off a number of explosives aboard Zodoh's [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]], the ''[[Voracious]]'', disrupting the coordination of the Stormdrivers.

The Stormdrivers still proved successful, and Zodoh soon turned his attention to Daiman's [[Capital/Legends|capital]] world of [[Darkknell/Legends|Darkknell]]. Although he caught Daiman's forces off-guard, Zodoh's [[Battle of Darkknell|attack]] on Darknell was foiled by Devaad and the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Kerra Holt]]. The ''Voracious'' was destroyed, effectively disabling the Stormdriver fleet, and Zodoh was left stranded in the [[Vacuum/Legends|vacuum]] of space. Following the battle, Zodoh was found injured but alive by Daiman's forces and taken before the Sith Lord, who used a miniature Stormdriver to exact revenge by dehydrating the Hutt.

==Biography==
===Crime lord===
{{Quote|Governments fall, but we remain. The Hutt clans have ways of talking to each other, of moving goods and muscle. The smarter Sith Lords realized that&mdash;and made a place at the table for us. The others&mdash;are no longer around.|Zodoh|<ref name="SWKE6" />}}
During the [[Republic Dark Age]], the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] was unable to afford to maintain its communications network and shut down [[comm-relay]]s outside the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> When the comm-relays in [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]] went down, the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]] were quick to take advantage, leaving the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]] operating in that part of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] reliant on the [[Kajidic/Legends|Hutt clans]] to move equipment and personnel. The Hutt [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] Zodoh was among those who profited by dealing in [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]] and munitions.<ref name="SWKE6" /> At some point, Zodoh's clan captured an entire Republic [[Task force/Legends|task force]]<ref name="SWKE7" /> on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Daalang/Legends|Daalang]] after the local population betrayed them. The captive Republic personnel were put to work as slaves in Zodoh's [[Prison/Legends|labor camps]].<ref name="SWKE8" /> However, after five [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of captivity, a small number of survivors, including [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Jenn Devaad]], escaped and joined [[Grace Command]], a mercy organization run by the [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaanian]] [[Baron/Legends|Baron]] [[Lemayne]],<ref name="SWKE7" /> which delivered supplies to those trapped in [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Realspace/Legends|space]].<ref name="SWKE6" />

During the later stages of the [[New Sith Wars]], Hutt Space was locked in internecine clan warfare with the Sith playing different clans against each other. Growing tired of the battling clans, Zodoh decided to expand his business operations beyond Hutt Space and turned his attention to the [[Grumani sector/Legends|Grumani sector]]<ref name="SWKE8" /> in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="EAO1">{{SW|url=news/essential-atlas-outer-rim-sectors|text=The Essential Atlas Extra: Outer Rim Sectors|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref> The Grumani [[Sector/Legends|sector]] had previously been controlled by the [[Chagras Hegemony]], a Sith state ruled the the Sith Lord [[Chagras]], but had descended into squabbling principalities since Chagras's [[Death/Legends|death]].<ref name="EAO2">{{SW|url=news/essential-atlas-extra-the-knight-errant-gazetter|text=Essential Atlas Extra: The Knight Errant Gazetteer|int=The Knight Errant Gazetteer}}</ref> Seeking to take advantage of the Sith infighting, Zodoh sought to establish a presence in the sector and sell his services to the warring Sith factions. As Zodoh began launching hit-and-run attacks on Sith forces, he discovered the true nature of Grace Command's missions in the area: the mercy organization served as a front for [[Operation Deluge]], an effort to sabotage the Sith war effort by inundating entire worlds with [[Deluge]],<ref name="SWKE8" /> an addictive [[Spice/Legends|drug]] which sapped all desire from those who took it.<ref name="SWKE6" />

===Imperial ambitions===
{{Quote|I've come here to spread the franchise. Make room for Zodoh&mdash;and you'll gain a key supplier of slaves and munitions. Resist&mdash;and you'll see I play even rougher than you do.|Zodoh tries to intimidate his Sith rivals|<ref name="SWKE6" />}}
[[File:Zodoh.jpg|thumb|left|220px|Zodoh offers a "business deal" to his Sith competitors.]]
By [[1032 BBY/Legends|1032 BBY]], Zodoh had consolidated a substantial [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] of military [[Starship/Legends|starships]] led by his [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]], the ''[[Voracious]]''.<ref name="SWKE6" /> Zodoh's fleet also included several [[Stormdriver]]s,<ref name="SWKE7" /> [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]] equipped with weaponized [[Moisture vaporator/Legends|moisture vaporators]] that were capable of generating downpours by squeezing moisture from a planet's [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]]. While the Sith [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Daiman]], ruler of an area of Sith space known as the [[Daimanate]], was away from his holdings to oversee the [[Invasion of the Bactranate|invasion]] of the nearby [[Bactranate]]<ref name="SWKE6" /> following the fall of the Sith Lord [[Ayanos Bactra]],<ref name="KE">[[Knight Errant (novel)|''Knight Errant'']]</ref> Zodoh saw the opportunity to launch an invasion of the Daimanate. Zodoh personally led a strike force consisting of [[Intruder-class starfighter|''Intruder''-class starfighters]] in an [[Battle of Capital Cay|attack]] on the Daimanate world of [[Aquilaris Minor]]. Emerging from [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] within the Sith patrol zones and immediately striking at the surface, the Hutt took the small military garrison at the [[Ocean/Legends|oceanic]] port of [[Capital Cay]] by surprise, inflicting heavy damage before the [[Sith trooper (New Sith Wars)|Sith troopers]] could mount a defense. With the Sith reeling from his initial attack, Zodoh withdrew his [[Starfighter/Legends|fighters]] and positioned [[Unidentified Stormdriver (Battle of Capital Cay)|one of his Stormdrivers]] over Capital Cay's bay, using its vaporators to start draining the [[Water/Legends|water]] from the bay. As a result, he triggered a storm which would flood Capital Cay and sweep the surviving Sith into the sea. Zodoh's attack coincided with the arrival on Aquilaris of the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Kerra Holt]], who was on a covert mission to liberate the planet's enslaved inhabitants. Finding the population addicted to Deluge and unwilling to assist her, Holt attacked the Stormdriver with a [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistol]]. With the crew preoccupied, the Stormdriver was ambushed and destroyed by [[Devil Squadron]], a [[Squadron/Legends|unit]] of [[Fire Lotus-class starfighter|''Fire Lotus''-class starfighters]] affiliated with Grace Command<ref name="SWKE6" /> and comprised of the Daalang survivors, led by Devaad.<ref name="SWKE7" /> Facing unexpected opposition, Zodoh withdrew his forces to the ''Voracious''.<ref name="SWKE6" />

Despite the loss of the Stormdriver, the attack on Aquilaris had proved a successful test of Zodoh's new weapons and provided sufficient data on Aquilaris's atmospheric systems for Zodoh to proceed to the next phase of his [[Aquilaris campaign|campaign]].<ref name="SWKE6" /> A single Stormdriver could produce a violent storm; by using his entire fleet of Stormdrivers, Zodoh could drain a planet's atmosphere of all moisture, drowning its entire population.<ref name="SWKE7" /> Back aboard the ''Voracious'', the Hutt convened a live [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]] conference with several Sith [[Warlord/Legends|warlords]] including [[Odion]], [[Arkadia Calimondra]]<ref name="SWKE6" /> and [[Malakite]].<ref name="SWKE6" /><ref name="JJM5">{{Faraway|url=comics/swknighterrantdeluge/swknighterrantdeluge5.html|text=''Star Wars: Knight Errant&mdash;Deluge #5''}}</ref> By expanding into Sith territory, Zodoh had incurred the wrath of the local Sith Lords, and both Odion and Calimondra expressed their anger at being summoned by the Hutt. In response, Zodoh accused the Sith Lords of the Grumani sector of being a bunch of petty crooks more interested in short-term gains than long-term strategic goals. Zodoh explained that he was in Sith space to expand his business franchise by selling slaves and munitions to the Sith warlords. The Hutt promised that those who cooperated with him would benefit as business partners, and reminded them that the Sith who had opposed the Hutts in Hutt Space were no longer around. In case the Sith Lords had any doubts, Zodoh instructed them to inform their [[Spy/Legends|spies]] in the Daimanate to watch for a demonstration of his abilities on Aquilaris. After concluding the meeting, Zodoh conferred with his trusted [[Advisor/Legends|advisor]], [[Oon Garat]], who expressed her distrust of the Hutt's potential Sith business partners. Zodoh, however, was confident that his planned demonstration would convince the Sith to ally themselves with him, and instructed Garat to dispatch a courier to the Hutt [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of [[Nal Hutta/Legends|Nal Hutta]] to report that he was ready for the next step in the operation.<ref name="SWKE6" />

===Reunion with an old foe===
{{Quote|Release my crew!''"<br />"''Already done, my dear Captain. While you were away, I released them&mdash;through the airlock.''"<br />"''You didn't have to do that!''"<br />"''They were escaped slaves, just like you. An entrepreneur must set certain standards. I am surprised, Devaad&mdash;you really should've known what to expect from me.|Devaad and Zodoh|<ref name="SWKE9">[[Knight Errant: Deluge 4|''Knight Errant: Deluge'' 4]]</ref>}}
[[File:Zodoh_vs_Jenn.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Zodoh confronts Jenn Devaad.]]
Meanwhile, Holt had joined up with Devil Squadron, and together they had finished pacifying the remaining Daimanate forces on Aqualaris. Zodoh's fleet returned to the [[Aquilaris Minor system/Legends|Aquilaris Minor system]] in time for the Hutt to witness Devil Squadron depart for the Malakite-occupied world of [[Heptooine]]. Flying one of his ''Intruder''-class starfighters, Zodoh allowed Devil Squadron to see him as they proceeded to their hyperspace jump point. Seeking vengeance for her period in captivity, Devaad ignored Holt's call for caution and led Devil Squadron in pursuit of the Hutt. Taunting Devaad via his [[Comm unit/Legends|comm unit]], Zodoh led his pursuers back to the waiting ''Voracious'' before ordering the launch of his starfighter squadrons. With the tables turned on the pursuers, Devaad ordered her starfighters to disengage from the [[Starfighter combat/Legends|dogfight]] and make for any jump point. At this moment, a large fleet of Stormdrivers emerged from hyperspace, [[Capture of Devil Squadron|trapping]] Devil Squadron in the [[Star system/Legends|system]].<ref name="SWKE7" />

As Zodoh boasted of his intentions to drown the people of Aquilaris as a demonstration of his power,<ref name="SWKE7" /> Holt suggested returning to Aquilaris to begin an evacuation. Devaad, however, was determined to get revenge against Zodoh and ignored the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi's]] advice, leading Devil Squadron in an [[Space warfare/Legends|attack]] on Zodoh's fleet of Stormdrivers. Zodoh was not unprepared for starfighter opposition, and his Stormdrivers were each equipped with defensive systems which prevented the outnumbered Grace Command fighters from inflicting serious damage. Within [[Standard minute/Legends|minutes]], Devil Squadron started to take losses. Seeing little strategic gain in assaulting Zodoh's fleet and unable to persuade Devaad to help her, Holt disengaged her starfighter, [[Devil Seven]], from the firefight and returned to Aquilaris. As a finale, Zodoh ordered the crew of the ''Voracious'' to activate the [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beam]] projector, using it to ensnare the surviving Devil Squadron starfighters. Brought aboard Zodoh's flagship, the squadron members were disarmed, imprisoned and [[Torture/Legends|tortured]] within the warship's holding cells.<ref name="SWKE8" />

Zodoh had Captain Devaad brought before him, held suspended with her wrists in [[Stuncuffs/Legends|stun cuffs]] while the Hutt gloated over his recent victory and his plans for the Grumani sector. Zodoh told Devaad that he had uncovered Grace Command's true purpose in Sith space.<ref name="SWKE8" /> The Hutt planned to turn Operation Deluge to his advantage by synthesizing his own stock of the drug and using it to lace supplies of seafood from Aquilaris which he would sell to the Sith. Zodoh intended to turn entire planetary populations into drug addicts, leaving nearby Sith worlds ripe for conquest while also making a profit from food relief.<ref name="SWKE9" /> Zodoh attempted to coerce Devaad into his service by offering to spare the lives of her [[Wingmate/Legends|wingmates]] if she cooperated in retrieving the stocks of the drug which Grace Command had recently delivered to Aquilaris. Devaad reluctantly agreed and was dispatched to the planet in a [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]], while Zodoh remained in [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] with the ''Voracious'' and his fleet of Stormdrivers.<ref name="SWKE8" />

Following a confrontation with her former ally Holt, Devaad returned to Zodoh's flagship in the shuttle with the remaining Deluge containers.<ref name="SWKE8" /> With the Deluge in his possession, Zodoh gave the green light for his fleet of Stormdrivers to [[Great Aquilaris Deluge|submerge]] Aquilaris in water. Within [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]], the planet's surface was flooded. The survivors, led by Holt and the [[Seacroppers' Guild|seacropper]] [[Joad Kreel]], managed to escape in a [[Submarine/Legends|submarine]] to a [[harvester station]] on the sea floor. In another holo-conference with his Sith rivals, Zodoh gloated over his new [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] which had resulted in the submergence of Capital Cay. He threatened to flood all of Lord Daiman's worlds, starting with his [[Capital/Legends|capital]], [[Darkknell/Legends|Darkknell]], which Zodoh intended to requisition as his own following Daiman's capitulation. The Hutt offered the Sith Lords the opportunity of becoming his trading partners if they agreed to keep Daiman's forces busy while he struck, and he threatened that those who did not join him would share Daiman's fate.<ref name="SWKE9" />

After concluding the holo-transmission, Zodoh was confronted by Devaad, who demanded that the Hutt honor his side of the bargain by releasing her captive crew. Zodoh, however, had never had any intention of releasing his [[Prisoner/Legends|prisoners]] and had already executed them by releasing them into space through the [[Airlock/Legends|airlock]], as an example to other slaves of the consequences of trying to escape. Devaad had prepared for this development and had rigged the Deluge containers with explosives from the [[Torpedo/Legends|torpedoes]] on Holt's Fire Lotus before returning to the ''Voracious''. She remotely detonated the explosives, causing a series of explosions throughout the ship. The blasts killed several of Zodoh's crew but did little damage to the ''Voracious'', with the exception of disrupting the coordination of the Stormdrivers which had already completed their task. Zodoh himself was sent flying into a bulkhead by a nearby blast. Although Zodoh survived due to his protective [[Armor/Legends|armor]], the distraction allowed Devaad to slip away and escape by stealing one of Zodoh's [[Zodoh's twin-seater starfighter|twin-seater starfighters]]. Unable to stop Devaad's escape, Zodoh recalled the Stormdrivers and ordered his fleet to depart for Darkknell.<ref name="SWKE9" />

===An untimely demise===
{{Quote|Daiman&mdash;Lord Daiman&mdash;I can see I've underestimated you. Perhaps we can make a deal&hellip;''"<br />"''You're already been dealing, Zodoh. Or is it a coincidence that the flow of Deluge into my territory stopped with your capture?|Zodoh tries to bargain with Daiman|<ref name="SWKE10">[[Knight Errant: Deluge 5|''Knight Errant: Deluge'' 5]]</ref>}}
[[File:Zodoh_and_Daiman.jpg|thumb|left|350px|Zodoh is tortured at the hands of Daiman.]]
Having purged half of his defense force due to the Deluge drug epidemic, and with his remaining [[Battleship/Legends|battleships]] called away to respond to incursions by his Sith rivals along the Daimanate's borders, Daiman was caught unprepared for Zodoh's arrival. The Hutt's fleet [[Battle of Darkknell|blockaded]] Darkknell, overwhelming Daiman's understaffed defense force, and the Stormdrivers moved into the atmosphere, triggering storms that submerged much of the planet, causing widespread damage and sweeping away anyone caught in the path of the flood water. Despite worldwide broadcasts by the Sith Lord trying to allay the fears of his subjects, Daiman was effectively powerless against the onslaught. The [[Southern Reservoir]] was unable to cope with the denudation and burst its banks, flooding [[Sanctum Celestial|Daiman's palace]] in the [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Xakrea]].<ref name="SWKE10" />

While Zodoh's victory seemed almost complete, he had underestimated Kerra Holt and Jenn Devaad. The Jedi Knight and Republic starfighter [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] teamed up to stop Zodoh's onslaught, using the stolen twin-seater Hutt starfighter to catch up to his fleet in orbit above Darkknell. Since the explosives that she had set off aboard the ''Voracious'' had disrupted the Stormdrivers' attack on Aquilaris, Devaad deduced that the Hutt lord's flagship contained a command center with a massive data processor for coordinating the Stormdrivers. Devaad flew the starfighter into the [[Hangar/Legends|hangar]] bay of Zodoh's flagship, allowing Holt to eject and infiltrate the vessel, before joining the fight against the Hutt's fleet. Holt quickly eliminated Zodoh's guards in the hangar and made her way to the control dome at the top of the vessel. Zodoh was overseeing the assault from the control dome when Holt arrived, and the Hutt surprised the Jedi with a blast of energy that sent her crashing to the deck and caused her to drop her [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]]. Clad in his armor and armed with an antique [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Vibro-ax/Legends|axe]], the Hutt chose to duel with Holt personally, disabling the [[Artificial gravity generator/Legends|artificial gravity]] and activating his [[Jetpack/Legends|jetpack]] to even the odds against the Jedi's [[Force power/Legends|Force abilities]].<ref name="SWKE10" />

Zodoh swung his axe at Holt, but the Jedi evaded the blow and [[Telekinesis/Legends|retrieved]] her lightsaber. Before she could bring her weapon to bear, however, Zodoh wrapped his tail around the Jedi and drew her to him, using his arms to crush her. Ready to deliver a killing blow, the Hutt was interrupted by Devaad's hijacked starfighter, which shot a hole through the control dome, resulting in an [[explosive decompression]]. Holt escaped in Devaad's fighter, but Zodoh and the control dome's crew were blown into space moments before a series of explosions destroyed the ''Voracious''. With the destruction of the ''Voracious'', the Stormdrivers were unable to coordinate their global storm, and Daiman's defense forces were able to regroup. The Sith Lord's forces found Zodoh clinging to the wreckage of the ''Voracious'' and were surprised to learn that he had survived, since his Hutt physique was tough enough to withstand exposure to the [[Vacuum/Legends|vacuum]] of space. The unconscious Hutt was captured by Daiman's [[Cruiser/Legends|cruisers]], stripped of his armor and brought as a captive before the Sith Lord.<ref name="SWKE10" />

Zodoh was bound in a purpose-built metal cradle while Daiman's agents revived him. When Zodoh regained consciousness, he found Daiman and several Sith guards standing over him. Also present via hologram were fellow Sith Lords Odion, Malakite and Arkadia Calimondra, who gloated over the change in his fortunes. Zodoh tried to plead with Daiman for his life by proposing a deal. Daiman, however, was unwilling to cooperate. Daiman wanted revenge for the brief spell of ignominy that he endured during the Battle of Darkknell and also blamed the Hutt for the flow of Deluge into his territory, since it had ceased with Zodoh's defeat. The Sith Lord explained that he had been studying Zodoh's Stormdriver technology. Although he considered the dependency on a large data processor to be a flaw which made the technology impractical on a planetary scale, Daiman had developed a miniature Stormdriver which was capable of completely draining all water from individual lifeforms, including Hutts. Daiman, who believed himself to be the creator of the [[Universe/Legends|universe]], dismissed Zodoh's creation as a mistake which he intended to correct and proceeded to use the device to dehydrate the Hutt.<ref name="SWKE10" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|I'm like no Hutt you've ever known, Human. I enjoy field work&mdash;getting my hands dirty. It's made me more effective than any of my kin&mdash;and much disliked. But what I'm doing in this sector will prove me the greatest Hutt of all.|Zodoh, to Kerra Holt|<ref name="SWKE10" />}}
[[File:Zodoh_vs_Kerra.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Zodoh battles Kerra Holt.]]
Zodoh was a [[Color/Legends|brown]]-skinned [[Gender/Legends|male]] Hutt with orange [[Eye/Legends|eyes]].<ref name="SWKE7" /> As was common among his species, Zodoh was involved in crime, primarily slave trading and munitions production, but viewed himself as a businessman providing services to his clients. The Hutt was quick to seize opportunities to expand his business. When the Republic turned off comm relays in Hutt Space, Zodoh saw the opportunity to provide logistical services to the Sith in that part of space.<ref name="SWKE6" /> When he later grew tired of the infighting between the Hutt clans,<ref name="SWKE8" /> Zodoh saw the opportunity to take advantage of the war between the Sith Lords in the Grumani sector, picking the Daimanate as a weak target in which to set up a presence while Lord Daiman's attention was focused elsewhere.<ref name="SWKE6" /> Upon learning about Grace Command's Operation Deluge, Zodoh planned to use the drug to further his own plans by tainting food supplies, destabilizing his enemies and allowing him to make a profit at the same time.<ref name="SWKE9" />

Zodoh did not trust others easily. His [[Aide/Legends|aide]], Oon Garat, was among the few beings in Zodoh's confidence, and the Hutt found that even she was targeted by rivals hoping to recruit her. As a result, Zodoh took an active role in his ventures, viewing this as the only way for him to guarantee success.<ref name="SWKE8" /> Unusually for a Hutt, Zodoh found that he enjoyed working in the field and that combat appealed to his hedonistic tendencies. Although his leadership style made him unpopular, Zodoh believed that it made him more effective than other Hutts. The Hutt could not resist the opportunity to try his hand at something new and was eager for the opportunity to test himself in combat against a Jedi.<ref name="SWKE10" />

Zodoh was arrogant, with ambitions of becoming the greatest Hutt of all.<ref name="SWKE10" /> He was not easily impressed and spoke dismissively to the Sith Lords in the Grumani sector, seeing them as little more than petty crooks and believing that they would come to serve him.<ref name="SWKE6" /> He was manipulative and deceptive, both in his dealings with the Sith<ref name="SWKE9" /> and with Devaad, whom he tricked into delivering a supply of Deluge to him by promising to spare the lives of the other Devil Squadron pilots,<ref name="SWKE8" /> when he instead planned to execute them as a warning to other slaves of the consequences of defying him. Zodoh had little regard for the lives of other [[Sentience/Legends|sentients]]. His callous nature was best exemplified by his willingness to addict entire populations to Deluge and his use of Stormdrivers to create artificial storms to drown his enemies. In order to conquer Darkknell, Zodoh was prepared to sacrifice many of its population of billions.<ref name="SWKE9" /> However, the Hutt was also cunning and patient, willing to accept small losses to achieve long-term objectives. This was evident in his acceptance of the loss of one Stormdriver during the attack on Capital Cay in return for gaining the necessary intelligence on Aqualaris Minor's atmospheric systems,<ref name="SWKE6" /> and his later willingness to abandon his Aquilaris campaign after Devaad's interference to focus on his main objective of attacking Darkknell.<ref name="SWKE9" />

==Skills and abilities==
{{Quote|I've waited for years for the chance to battle a Jedi on equal terms. In here, with my armor's control jets&mdash;and this Mandalorian antique&mdash;I'm going to get my wish!|Zodoh|<ref name="SWKE10" />}}
As opposed to most other members of his species, Zodoh was a physically fit fighter.<ref name="SWKE9" /> The Hutt wore armor over his upper body and a jetpack which allowed him to fly.<ref name="SWKE7" /> He enjoyed dueling with his opponents using his weapon of choice, an antique Mandalorian axe. Zodoh could also use his own body as a weapon, employing his large physical mass to subdue and overpower his opponents and wrapping his muscular tail around opponents in order to draw them to him and crush them. With his jetpack providing an advantage in zero [[Gravity/Legends|gravity]], Zodoh proved a match for the Jedi Kerra Holt. His Hutt physiology allowed him to survive in space after the destruction of the ''Voracious'' whereas most species would have been killed.<ref name="SWKE10" /> Zodoh was a skilled pilot and often led his ''Intruder''-class starfighter squadrons into battle,<ref name="SWKE6" /><ref name="SWKE7" /> lying forward in his starfighter with his [[Limb/Legends|arms]] operating controls in the wings.<ref name="JJM2">{{Faraway|url=comics/swknighterrantdeluge/swknighterrantdeluge2.html|text=Star Wars: Knight Errant &ndash; Deluge #2}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Zodoh was created by author [[John Jackson Miller]] and artist [[Ivan Rodriguez]]<ref name="JJM1">{{Faraway|url=comics/swknighterrantdeluge/swknighterrantdeluge1.html|text=''Star Wars: Knight Errant&mdash;Deluge #1''}}</ref> to serve as a key antagonist in the [[Star Wars: Knight Errant: Deluge|''Deluge'' story arc]] of the [[Star Wars: Knight Errant (comic series)|''Star Wars: Knight Errant'']] [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] series. The character first appeared in [[Knight Errant: Deluge 1|''Knight Errant: Deluge'' 1]],<ref name="SWKE6" /> released on [[August 17]], [[2011]],<ref name="DH">{{DarkHorse|url=Blog/321/2011-year-star-wars|text=2011: The Year of Star Wars}}</ref> and subsequently appeared in all issues within the ''Deluge'' story arc, in which he was illustrated by Rodriguez, [[Iban Coello]], [[Sergio Abad]], and [[David Daza]].<ref name="SWKE6" /><ref name="SWKE7" /><ref name="SWKE8" /><ref name="SWKE9" /><ref name="SWKE10" /> Miller created Zodoh after seeing in ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' by [[Jason Fry]] and [[Daniel Wallace]] that Hutt Space was under Sith control during the period in which ''Knight Errant'' is set. When Fry confirmed that no backstory had yet been created to explain the relationship between the Hutts and the Sith, Miller decided to include a Hutt character in ''Knight Errant''.<ref name="JJM1" /> Although Daiman announces his intention to completely dehydrate Zodoh after his capture at the end of [[Knight Errant: Deluge 5|''Knight Errant: Deluge'' 5]], Zodoh's death has not been confirmed in any source.<ref name="SWKE10" />
